basis: Eye, dental and cardiac defects define OFCD; skeletal contractures/synostosis occur in 30-79%. Intellectual disability reported in 1/3 is omitted under the four-axis cap.
Congenital communication between atrial chambers; stroke and respiratory complications are uncommon or separately diagnosed.
Defined by cerebellar injury causing cerebral palsy and ataxia; impaired movement alone does not establish primary muscle damage.
Diaphragmatic muscle defects and cardiac malformations define the syndrome; pulmonary hypoplasia occurs in 10/13. Genital malformations have no axis.
Molecular subtype of medulloblastoma, a malignant cerebellar/CNS tumor.
Disease specifically located in the retinal nerve fiber layer; retinal neural tissue belongs to the ocular axis.
Progressive white-matter disease with deafness reported in 7/7; anemia in 3/7 supports blood involvement. Renal insufficiency 2/7 falls below 30%; lactate alone adds no axis.
Fungal infection directly occupies and damages the toenail.
Inherited ammonia-detoxification defect; hyperammonemic brain injury and lasting neurodevelopmental impairment affect approximately 30-60%, varying with severity.
PRPF6-related retinal degeneration with rod-cone dystrophy, visual-field loss and impaired acuity.
Embryonal soft-tissue sarcoma with skeletal-muscle differentiation; mucosal sites vary across the group, so no additional organ site is assigned.
Odontomas and esophageal obstruction define the syndrome; supplied phenotypes report hepatic failure and atherosclerosis each in 80-99%.
Defined by oral malformations: cleft palate 22/27, cleft lip 15/27 and lip pits 14/27; lips, palate and teeth map to gastrointestinal.
Inherited magnesium-transport disorder, predominantly a renal tubular reabsorption defect. Intestinal dysfunction is subtype-dependent; nephrocalcinosis is not universal.
Defining nasal alar cartilage defects map to pulmonary; cleft upper lip occurs in 80-99%. Telecanthus and hypertelorism do not establish eye damage.
Oral disorder defined by tooth grinding and jaw clenching; teeth belong to gastrointestinal. Clenching alone does not establish muscle or CNS injury.
GPI biosynthesis defect with severe neurodevelopmental disease; scoliosis 5/5 and ocular misalignment 5/5 support involvement. Cerebral visual impairment is neurologic.
Factor IX gain of function causes a coagulation disorder; venous thrombosis is a separately diagnosed consequence rather than inherent vascular injury.
Moyamoya is progressive cerebral arterial stenosis; ischemic brain injury and stroke affect more than 30% over the typical course.
Spastic neurodevelopmental disease within P5CS amino-acid metabolism deficiency. Muscle wasting 4/6 and incontinence reflect neural dysfunction; cataract 1/6 is below threshold.
Intellectual disability, epilepsy and postaxial polydactyly define the syndrome; dental abnormalities and contractures are occasional.
Progressive encephalopathy and optic atrophy define PEHO. Contractures may follow immobility; gingival overgrowth lacks clear treatment-independent injury evidence.
Mitochondrial respiratory-chain metabolic disorder; encephalopathy/developmental impairment affects >30%. Hepatic, cardiac and intrinsic muscle injury vary across subtypes.
Infectious abscess directly destroys lung parenchyma.
Familial middle-ear ossicular malformations cause conductive hearing impairment; ear ossicles belong to otologic rather than musculoskeletal.
